questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A 42-year-old man with history of alcohol dependency presents with progressive abdominal distension. Abdominal examination reveals shifting dullness. Which one of the following is the most appropriate drug to relieve this abdominal distension?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Spironolactone

The patient has ascites secondary to alcoholic liver cirrhosis with portal hypertension, as suggested by progressive abdominal distension and shifting dullness. The first-line pharmacological treatment for cirrhotic ascites is spironolactone, an aldosterone antagonist, because secondary hyperaldosteronism is the primary mechanism of sodium and water retention in cirrhosis.

In liver cirrhosis:

• Portal hypertension causes splanchnic vasodilation and reduced effective arterial blood volume.
• This activates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), leading to secondary hyperaldosteronism.
• Spironolactone blocks aldosterone, promoting sodium excretion and reducing ascites.

Why not the other options?

• A. Octreotide: Used in acute variceal bleeding and some cases of hepatorenal syndrome, not for routine management of ascites.
• B. Propranolol: A non-selective β-blocker used for primary and secondary prophylaxis of esophageal variceal bleeding, not for treating ascites.
• C. Lactulose: Used for the treatment and prevention of hepatic encephalopathy by reducing ammonia absorption; it does not relieve ascites.
questions.learning: Spironolactone — The patient has ascites secondary to alcoholic liver cirrhosis with portal hypertension, as suggested by progressive abdominal distension and shifting dullness.

questions.subject: Paediatrics
questions.text: A child with sore throat starts developing skin lesions as in the image below. Which of the following is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Guttate psoriasis is a distinct form of psoriasis characterized by the sudden eruption of small, drop-like, scaly papules and plaques across the trunk and limbs. It is strongly associated with a preceding Group A Streptococcal infection (such as a sore throat or tonsillitis) roughly 2–3 weeks prior. The word "guttate" is derived from the Latin word for "drop." Pustular psoriasis (Option B) involves sterile pustules and is a much more severe, potentially systemic condition. Erythrodermic psoriasis (Option C) involves generalized redness and scaling of over 90% of the body surface area and is a medical emergency. Inverse psoriasis (Option D) occurs in skin folds (axillae, groin) and lacks the characteristic "drop" distribution. In many children and young adults, guttate psoriasis may resolve spontaneously or evolve into the more common plaque-type psoriasis. Treatment usually involves management of the underlying infection and topical steroids or phototherapy
questions.learning: Guttate psoriasis is a distinct form of psoriasis characterized by the sudden eruption of small, drop-like, scaly papules and plaques across the trunk and limbs.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: What will be the line of management for the condition shown in the image given below?
questions.explanation: The image shows a well-defined, smooth, rounded swelling at the medial aspect of the upper eyelid — classic appearance of a dermoid cyst, which is a benign choristomatous lesion commonly occurring at the superomedial or superolateral orbital rim in young patients. Key Clinical Features visible: 1. Well-circumscribed, smooth swelling 2. Located near medial canthus/orbital rim 3. Non-inflammatory appearance 4. No overlying skin changes Treatment: Complete surgical excision is the definitive treatment. The cyst must be removed intact to prevent recurrence and inflammatory reaction from cyst contents spillage. Why other options are wrong: (B) Radiotherapy is incorrect because dermoid cysts are benign lesions — radiotherapy is reserved for malignant tumors. It has absolutely no role in managing benign orbital cysts. (C) Antibiotics is incorrect because dermoid cysts are non-infectious developmental anomalies, not bacterial infections. Antibiotics have no therapeutic effect on cystic lesions of this nature. (D) International steroids is incorrect because steroid injections are used for chalazion or inflammatory lesions. Dermoid cysts have a true epithelial lining requiring complete surgical removal — steroids cannot resolve them

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.text: A 22-year-old male was brought to the emergency room following a road traffic accident. On examination, his GCS was E2M2V3. He had no fractures and no hydrocephalus or raised intracranial pressure. Non-contrast CT was performed and was found to be normal. The likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Diffuse axonal injury

The given clinical scenario of an RTA with no imaging abnormality along with a disproportionate clinical manifestation suggests diffuse axonal injury.

It is caused due to stretching of axons in subcortical white matter due to sudden deceleration injuries. It is usually associated with mild nonspecific changes in NCCT. It is visualized on T2 MRI characterized by multiple lesions showing microbleeds or linear hypointensities. It may also show disruption of white matter tracts on tractography.

Other options

Post-concussion syndrome usually follows mild traumatic brain injury. It does not have a severe clinical status as seen in this patient.

Extradural hemorrhage is produced usually results secondary to trauma to head. The bleeding is usually arterial and blood collects between outer dura and inner table of the skull. It can very well be visualized on CT.

A cerebral herniation is defined as a shift of cerebral tissue in an adjacent space. Intracranial brain herniation can be classified into 3 types - subfalcine, transtentorial and tonsillar. A distinct clinical picture can be produced as a result of compression of neurovascular structures by the herniating part. CT is the imaging modality of choice because it can be done rapidly.
questions.learning: Diffuse axonal injury — The given clinical scenario of an RTA with no imaging abnormality along with a disproportionate clinical manifestation suggests diffuse axonal injury.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text: A 32-year-old female presents with progressive bilateral hearing loss, in the right ear more than left. After the initial evaluation, a stapedotomy of the right ear was planned. What might've been the tuning fork test results of the patient?
options: Bilateral Rinne's negative, Weber's lateralized to the right
Bilateral Rinne's negative, Weber's lateralized to the left
Bilateral Rinne's positive, Weber's lateralized to the right
Bilateral Rinne's positive, Weber's lateralized to the left
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Bilateral Rinne's negative, Weber's lateralized to the right

In the given clinical scenario, a female with progressive bilateral hearing loss, in the right ear more than the left, and a stapedotomy of the right ear was planned. Stapedotomy surgery is done for otosclerosis. Otosclerosis results in conductive hearing loss so, the tuning fork test results of the patient will be Bilateral Rinne's negative, Weber's lateralized to the right.

As there is conductive hearing loss in both ears, like that associated with otosclerosis (which may require a stapedotomy), the bilateral Rinne test will be negative. In Weber's test, the sound lateralizes to the affected ear, which, in this case, is the right ear with more significant hearing loss.

Tuning fork tests are performed commonly with tuning forks of frequencies such as 128, 256, 512, 1024, etc. The tuning fork of 512 Hz is considered ideal as forks of lower frequencies produce a sense of bone vibration, while those of higher frequencies have a shorter decay time.

Rinne’s test is done by placing a vibrating tuning fork on the patient’s mastoid and when he stops hearing, it is brought beside the external auditory meatus (EAC). If he still hears the sound, air conduction (AC) is better than bone conduction (BC) i.e. AC>BC. The inferences are as follows:

• Rinne's test is considered positive (normal) when the air conduction AC>BC is seen in normal people and people with sensorineural deafness.
• It is considered negative when the BC>AC, and is seen in patients with conductive deafness.

Weber test is done by placing a vibrating tuning in the middle of the forehead or the vertex and the patient is asked in which ear the sound is heard. The inferences are as follows:

• Normal result is achieved when the sound heard equally in both ears
• In conductive deafness, it is lateralized to the worse ear
• In sensorineural deafness, it is lateralized to the better ear.
questions.learning: Bilateral Rinne's negative, Weber's lateralized to the right In the given clinical scenario, a female with progressive bilateral hearing loss, in the right ear more than the left, and a stapedotomy of the right ear was planned.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In Kaplan Meier survival curve, the bands used for the confidence interval is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hall-Wellner Band

The bands used for confidence interval in the Kaplan-Meier survival curve are Hall-Wellner bands.

When using standard statistical software, at each point in time, the upper and lower limits of the confidence interval are also obtained. Hall-Wellner bands, Gill bands, and Nair's Equal Precision confidence bands are used for this purpose.

Kaplan-Meier plot is a graphical representation of the number of people surviving during a given length of time. Often there are two or more groups represented in the plot, such as those treated versus those not treated. The graph often has a number of steps as the number of people surviving is a discrete variable. The image given below shows a Kaplan-Meier plot. The dotted lines represent the upper and lower limits of the 95% confidence interval.
questions.learning: Hall-Wellner Band — The bands used for confidence interval in the Kaplan-Meier survival curve are Hall-Wellner bands. When using standard statistical software, at each point in time, the upper and lower limits of the confidence interval are also obtained.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text: A patient with poorly controlled diabetes (HbA1c = 10) presents with severe, excruciating ear pain accompanied by blood-stained ear discharge. Based on this clinical presentation, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Necrotizing (malignant) otitis externa is a severe, life-threatening infection of the external auditory canal with extension to the skull base, occurring predominantly in elderly patients with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus or in those who are immuno compromised. Poor glycemic control is the most important predisposing factor. The hallmark clinical features include severe, deep-seated otalgia (often worse at night), persistent otorrhea that may be blood-stained, and the presence of granulation tissue at the junction of the cartilaginous and bony portions of the external auditory canal, which is a key diagnostic clue. Simple otitis externa (Option A) is a superficial infection and lacks systemic severity. Serous otitis media (Option C) involves sterile middle-ear effusion and is typically painless. Otomycosis (Option D) is a fungal infection presenting with itching and debris resembling wet newspaper, without invasive features. The most common causative organism is Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Untreated disease can progress to skull base osteomyelitis, leading to cranial nerve palsies and potentially meningitis. Diagnosis is supported by CT or MRI showing bony erosion. Management requires prolonged intravenous anti-pseudomonal antibiotics along with strict glycemic control

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pyometra

Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to pyometra. This refers to the collection of pus in the uterine cavity.

The initial infection involves the cervix uteri and urethra which may extend to Bartholin glands, skene glands, endometrium, and fallopian tubes. Unilateral pain and swelling over the labia may be caused by the inflammation of the Bartholin glands.

Depending on the extent of tissue involved, PID can be classified into five stages

• Stage I - Acute salpingitis without peritonitis - No adhesions
• Stage II - Acute salpingitis with peritonitis - purulent discharge
• Stage III - Acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo ovarian complex
• Stage IV - Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess
• Stage V - Tubercular salpingitis

Long-standing pelvic inflammation may also lead to:

• Dyspareunia
• Infertility
• Ectopic pregnancy
• Formation of adhesions like hydrosalpinx, pyosalpinx, tubo-ovarian abscess
• Chronic pelvic pain

Note: Chronic pelvic inflammation leads to dense adhesions between the uterus and the appendages. Thus, it becomes difficult to define the uterus from the pelvic masses. They form a hard mass which is called the frozen pelvis.

The most common cause of the spread of PID: Ascending infection along with sperms
The only PID that does not spread with the sexual route is genital TB. It has a hematogenous spread.
The most common PID in virgin females is genital TB.
Investigation of choice in PID: Abdominal USG
The surest sign of salpingitis is pus extruding from the fimbrial end of the tube.
questions.learning: Pyometra Long-standing pelvic inflammation may lead to pyometra. This refers to the collection of pus in the uterine cavity.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Prolactin level is highest during :
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 24 hours after delivery

Among the given options, the prolactin level is highest 24 hours after delivery.

The maximum level of prolactin is seen during pregnancy and in the immediate postpartum period. During pregnancy, the secretion is increased reaching a peak at the time of delivery. After delivery, the plasma concentration falls to nonpregnant levels in a few weeks. Suckling produces surges of prolactin release.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.text: Which muscle serves as the yoke muscle for the right lateral rectus?
questions.explanation: Yoke muscles, also known as contralateral synergists, are pairs of muscles—one in each eye—that work together to move both eyes simultaneously in the same direction (conjugate gaze). According to Hering's law of equal innervation, when a command for a version movement is sent, both muscles in the yoke pair receive equal nervous stimulation. For rightward horizontal gaze (dextroversion), the right lateral rectus must contract to abduct the right eye, while the left medial rectus must contract to adduct the left eye. Thus, the left medial rectus is the yoke muscle for the right lateral rectus. The right superior oblique (Option A) is involved in depression and intorsion. The left lateral rectus (Option C) is the yoke muscle for the right medial rectus during leftward gaze. The right medial rectus (Option D) is the antagonist to the right lateral rectus in the same eye. Understanding these pairings is essential for diagnosing paralytic strabismus and identifying which cranial nerves or muscles are dysfunctional during clinical motility testing
questions.learning: Yoke muscles, also known as contralateral synergists, are pairs of muscles—one in each eye—that work together to move both eyes simultaneously in the same direction (conjugate gaze).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which anatomical structure is located approximately 25 cm from the central incisor?
questions.explanation: According to many clinical/endoscopic sources (as in your key), the cricopharynx (upper esophageal sphincter) is located approximately 25 cm from the central incisors. It marks the junction of the pharynx and esophagus and acts as a functional sphincter preventing air entry during respiration and reflux during swallowing. It is also a key site evaluated in conditions like dysphagia and Zenker’s diverticulum. Why other options are incorrect: (B) Arch of Aorta: This produces a physiological constriction slightly lower, around 30 cm, not at 25 cm in this reference system. (C) Left principal bronchus: It crosses the esophagus at about 35 cm, causing another constriction, but is located further down. (D) Diaphragm: The esophageal hiatus is found at 40–45 cm, representing the lowest constriction near the gastroesophageal junction

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a normal distribution, the mean value is 82 and SD is 1.5. Calculate the range of 2 SD. SD-Standard deviation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 79 to 85

The range of 2 standard deviations for the given mean value is 79 to 85.

To determine the range within two standard deviations in a normal distribution, we use the formula:

Range= Mean ±2 × Standard Deviation (SD)

Given data: Mean = 82, Standard Deviation = 1.5.

2 SD = mean +/- 2 SD.

Calculation:
Lower limit=82−(2×1.5)=82−3=79.

Upper limit=82+(2×1.5)=82+3=85.

The range within two standard deviations is 79 to 85. This means approximately 95.4% of the values in a normal distribution fall within this range.

Pearl PF0301: Normal Distribution

* Normal distribution is the most widely used continuous distribution.

* It is also called bell curve (bell shaped) or Gaussian distribution after a mathematician named Karl Friedrich Gauss.

* The following is an image of three different types of normal distributions.

* Normal distributions are defined by two parameters: the mean and the standard deviation.

* The mean, median and mode are all equal in a normal distribution.

* All normal distributions are symmetric and have bell-shaped density curves with a single peak.

* Exactly half of the values are to the left of the centre and the other half to the right.

* The total area under the curve is 1.

* The density of a normal distribution is more around the centre and less around the tails.

* There is no skew in the curve.

* Looking at the figure below, we can understand the empirical rule of a normal distribution which states that:

* Approximately 68% of the distribution falls within one standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 1 SD).

* Approximately 95% of the distribution falls within two standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 2 SD).

* Approximately 99.7% of the distribution falls within three standard deviations of the mean (mean ± 3 SD).

* Many data like blood pressure, heights, IQ scores, etc. form a normal distribution.

* A standard normal distribution is a normal distribution with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A 60-year-old patient presents with dyspnea and chest pain. The pleural fluid analysis shows pleural protein/ serum protein > 0.5, and pleural LDH/ serum LDH > 0.4. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Tuberculosis

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an exudative pleural effusion according to Light's criteria. Among the given options, tuberculosis can lead to exudative pleural effusion.

In any patient diagnosed with a pleural effusion, an effort should be made to find the cause. This requires a diagnostic thoracocentesis and analysis of the pleural fluid in terms of whether it is a transudate or an exudate based on Light's criteria:

1. Pleural fluid protein/serum protein >0.5
2. Pleural fluid LDH/serum LDH >0.6
3. Pleural fluid LDH is more than two-thirds the upper limit of normal for serum

If the pleural fluid meets one of these criteria, it is considered exudative pleural effusion. Sometimes, special investigations like ADA and cytology might be required to rule out tuberculosis and malignancy respectively.

For thoracocentesis, a posterior approach is preferred. The patient should sit on the edge of the bed, leaning forward with the arms abducted onto a pillow on a bedside stand. The patient might have severe dyspnea, so it is important to assess whether they can maintain this position for 10 minutes before performing the procedure. The entry site for the thoracocentesis is at the superior aspect of the rib. This prevents any injury to the intercostal nerve and vessels.

While maintaining gentle negative pressure, the needle should be slowly advanced into the pleural space. If a diagnostic tap is being performed, 30-50 mL of fluid will be adequate. If a therapeutic thoracocentesis is being performed, a maximum of 1 litre of pleural fluid should be withdrawn at a given time. Withdrawal of quantities more than this can cause re-expansion pulmonary edema. A chest radiograph should be obtained post-procedure to evaluate for a pneumothorax. The patient should be instructed to inform the doctors if new shortness of breath develops.

Other options

Option A and C: Congestive heart failure and liver cirrhosis lead to transudative pleural effusion.
questions.learning: Tuberculosis — The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an exudative pleural effusion according to Light's criteria. Among the given options, tuberculosis can lead to exudative pleural effusion.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient is brought to the emergency department unconscious. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis shows: pH 7.1, PCO₂ 23 mmHg, PO₂ 98 mmHg, HCO₃ 16 mEq/L. What does this ABG indicate about the patient’s acid-base status?
questions.explanation: The ABG analysis reveals a pH of 7.1, which indicates significant academia. The bicarbonate (HCO3) level of 16 mEq/L is low (normal is 22–26 mEq/L), which is the primary cause of the low pH, thus defining metabolic acidosis. The low PCO2 of 23 mmHg (normal is 35–45 mmHg) indicates that the patient is hyperventilating to blow off carbon dioxide as a secondary "respiratory compensation" for the metabolic acid load. In respiratory acidosis (Option C), the pH would be low but the PCO2 would be high. In metabolic alkalosis (Option B) or respiratory alkalosis (Option D), the pH would be elevated above 7.45. Common causes for this severe metabolic acidosis in an unconscious patient include diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), lactic acidosis (from shock or sepsis), or toxic ingestions like aspirin or ethylene glycol
questions.learning: The ABG analysis reveals a pH of 7.1, which indicates significant academia. The bicarbonate (HCO3) level of 16 mEq/L is low (normal is 22–26 mEq/L), which is the primary cause of the low pH, thus defining metabolic acidosis.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient with malignancy develops humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy. Arrange the following steps in the appropriate sequence of management. 1. IV saline hydration to promote calciuresis 2. Bisphosphonate therapy 3. Loop diuretics after hydration 4. Find the source of exogenous ca
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 4, 1, 3, 2

Hypercalcemia of malignancy is a medical emergency. Initial management focuses on eliminating factors that worsen hypercalcemia, restoring intravascular volume, promoting renal calcium excretion, and inhibiting bone resorption.

The correct sequence of management is:

1. Stop external calcium intake and discontinue drugs that aggravate hypercalcemia (e.g., thiazides, vitamin D supplements, lithium).
2. IV normal saline hydration to correct dehydration and enhance urinary calcium excretion.
3. Loop diuretics (only after adequate hydration and if clinically indicated) to further increase calciuresis.
4. IV bisphosphonates (e.g., zoledronic acid, pamidronate) to inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and provide sustained calcium reduction.

Why not the other options?

• Hydration must precede loop diuretics to avoid worsening volume depletion.
• Bisphosphonates are not immediate-acting and should be administered after initial stabilization with hydration.
questions.learning: 4, 1, 3, 2 Hypercalcemia of malignancy is a medical emergency. Initial management focuses on eliminating factors that worsen hypercalcemia, restoring intravascular volume, promoting renal calcium excretion, and inhibiting bone resorption.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A girl diagnosed with schizophrenia presents to a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in India. Which Government of India (GOI)–provided online application is used to support mental health services in this setting?
questions.explanation: Tele-MANAS (Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States) is the correct application launched by the Government of India. It is a 24/7 toll-free service (14416) designed to provide immediate mental health support and counseling to individuals in distress. It aims to bridge the mental health care gap across all states. U-WIN (Option B) is a platform for tracking immunizations. NIKUSHT (Option C) is a digital platform for monitoring leprosy or sickle cell disease. NIKSHAY (Option D) is the national surveillance and reporting system for tuberculosis management. Given that the patient requires mental health support for schizophrenia, Tele-MANAS is the only relevant technical platform provided by the GOI for this specific clinical need

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child was brought to you with complaints of fever, malaise and a rash. You diagnose the child with measles. What is the recommended period of isolation for this disease?
options: From onset of rash to 3 days after rash
2 weeks before rash to 1 week after rash
From onset of rash to 5 days after rash
From catarrhal stage to 5 days after rash
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. From catarrhal stage to 5 days after rash

The isolation period for measles is from the catarrhal (prodromal) stage to 5 days after the onset of the rash.

The period of communicability is approximately 4 days before and 5 days after the appearance of the rash. Isolation of the patient for a week from the onset of rash adequately covers the period of communicability.
questions.learning: From catarrhal stage to 5 days after rash — The isolation period for measles is from the catarrhal (prodromal) stage to 5 days after the onset of the rash.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 44-year-old woman presents with a palpable flank mass measuring 4 cm on CT imaging, and urine examination reveals malignant cells. What is the most appropriate management for this condition?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation of a flank mass and malignant cells in the urine is strongly suggestive of a Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC). For small renal masses (typically defined as those less than 4 cm, or T1a tumors), "partial nephrectomy" (nephron-sparing surgery) is the preferred standard of care. This procedure removes the tumor while preserving as much healthy kidney tissue as possible, which helps maintain long-term renal function and reduces the risk of chronic kidney disease without compromising oncological outcomes compared to radical nephrectomy. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Option B) is not a standard treatment for localized RCC as these tumors are largely chemoresistant. Radical nephrectomy (Option C), the removal of the entire kidney, is reserved for larger, more complex, or centrally located tumors where a partial approach is not feasible. Postoperative radiotherapy (Option D) has a very limited role in RCC management. Therefore, given the small 4 cm size and the patient's relatively young age, partial nephrectomy is the most suitable and recommended intervention

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman, G1P1, presents with intermenstrual bleeding for the past 1.5 months. What is the initial investigation of choice?
questions.explanation: In any woman of reproductive age presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding, including intermenstrual bleeding, the absolute first step in management is to rule out pregnancy. A urine pregnancy test (UPT) is a rapid, cost-effective, and highly sensitive initial investigation that guides all subsequent diagnostic paths. Bleeding in a 28-year-old could be related to pregnancy complications such as a threatened abortion or ectopic pregnancy. Transvaginal ultrasound (Option B) is an excellent follow-up tool to visualize pelvic pathology like fibroids or polyps but is secondary to confirming pregnancy status. Abdominal ultrasound (Option A) is less sensitive for early gynecological issues than TVS. Endometrial biopsy (Option D) is generally reserved for women over 45 or those with significant risk factors for malignancy, which this patient lacks. Therefore, ruling out gestation remains the standard of care for the initial workup of abnormal bleeding
questions.learning: In any woman of reproductive age presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding, including intermenstrual bleeding, the absolute first step in management is to rule out pregnancy.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: During fasting, through which metabolic pathway does glucagon stimulate the production of glucose?
questions.explanation: During a fasting state, blood glucose levels drop, triggering the secretion of glucagon from the pancreatic alpha cells. Glucagon acts primarily on the liver to elevate blood glucose through two key metabolic pathways. First, it stimulates glycogenolysis, which is the breakdown of stored glycogen into glucose. Second, it promotes gluconeogenesis, the synthesis of new glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors like amino acids and glycerol. Glycolysis (Option A) is the breakdown of glucose to produce energy and is inhibited by glucagon to conserve glucose. Glycogenesis (Option C) is the synthesis of glycogen for storage, which occurs in the fed state under the influence of insulin. While gluconeogenesis (Option D) is a major contributor, it does not work alone; both pathways are essential for glucose homeostasis during fasting. Therefore, the combination of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis is the correct physiological response to glucagon
questions.learning: During a fasting state, blood glucose levels drop, triggering the secretion of glucagon from the pancreatic alpha cells. Glucagon acts primarily on the liver to elevate blood glucose through two key metabolic pathways.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following type of renal calculi is resistant to the extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cystine

Cystine stones are resistant to extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (ESWL) due to their hardness. Cystine, brushite, and calcium oxalate monohydrate stones are the most refractory to ESWL fragmentation, with cystine and brushite being the most resistant.

ESWL is a non-invasive method that generates shockwaves outside the body that focus on the stones. It is the most common method of treating urinary tract stones nowadays. Stones up to approximately 1.5 cm in size are suitable for this form of treatment.

Complications: Infection, haematuria, parenchymal hemorrhage, and perirenal hematoma.

Contraindications: Obese patients, pregnant patients, and patients taking oral anticoagulants.

Note: Stone fragments collecting in the distal ureter following ESWL are known as steinstrasse.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The hormone acting on post ovulatory endometrium is :
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Progesterone

The hormone acting on the post-ovulatory endometrium is progesterone.

Endometrium undergoes changes (endometrial cycle) during the menstrual cycle due to the action of various hormones. The basal zone (lower 1/3rd of the endometrium in contact with the myometrium) is uninfluenced by hormones and shows no change during the cycle. The rest (functional zone) shows the following changes:

1. Regenerative phase (first 2 to 3 days)- the regeneration of glands and the stromal cells from the basal zone. Endometrial thickness is about 2mm.
2. Proliferative phase (5 or 6th day to 14th day) - estrogen (option D) causes the glands to become more tubular and perpendicular to the surface and increases the thickness to 10-12mm on the 14th day (at the time of ovulation)
3. Secretory phase(15th day till menstrual bleeding) - post ovulation, estrogen-primed endometrium is acted by progesterone (from corpus lutetium) and causes increased blood flow (spiraling of arteries) and increases tortuosity of glands (saw-toothed/cork-screwed glands). The thickness of the endometrium is maximum (12mm) in this phase.
4. Menstruation (last 4 or 5 days) - estrogen and progesterone are withdrawn due to the regression of corpus luteum (lack of fertilization). This results in the shedding of the functional zone (menstrual bleeding).

Other options:

Option A: The luteinizing hormone (LH) is secreted by the anterior pituitary and is crucial for ovulation to occur on the 14th day of the menstrual cycle.

Option B: Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) is secreted by the anterior pituitary. The ovarian follicle with the most sensitivity to FSH becomes the dominant follicle for the current cycle and the rest undergo autolysis.
questions.learning: Progesterone — The hormone acting on the post-ovulatory endometrium is progesterone. Endometrium undergoes changes (endometrial cycle) during the menstrual cycle due to the action of various hormones.

questions.subject: Orthopaedics
questions.text: Finkelstein’s sign/test is done to diagnose which one of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. de Quervain’s tenosynovitis

Finkelstein’s test is used to diagnose de Quervain’s tenosynovitis, which involves inflammation of the first dorsal compartment tendons:

• Abductor pollicis longus (APL)
• Extensor pollicis brevis (EPB)

A positive test produces pain over the radial styloid when the thumb is flexed into the palm and the wrist is deviated ulnarly.

Why not other options?

• A. Adhesive capsulitis: Diagnosed by restriction of both active and passive shoulder movements.
• B. Golfer’s elbow: Medial epicondylitis; pain with resisted wrist flexion/pronation.
• C. Trochanteric bursitis: Causes lateral hip pain and tenderness over the greater trochanter.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to BMW rules, in which color-coded bag should the object shown in the image be discarded?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Red

Understand the Biomedical Waste Management (BMWM) Rules, 2016 (amended) and identify the correct color-coded container for disposal of contaminated healthcare waste. The item shown is an IV fluid/TPN bag, which is a contaminated recyclable plastic item. Such plastic waste should be discarded in the red bag for disinfection (autoclaving/microwaving/hydroclaving) followed by recycling.

Why not the other options?

• A. Red: ✔ Correct. Used for contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as IV sets, tubing, catheters, urine bags, syringes (without needles), gloves, and IV fluid bags.
• B. Yellow: Used for incinerable waste such as human anatomical waste, soiled waste, microbiological waste, expired medicines, and pathological waste.
• C. Blue: Used for glassware and metallic implants, including glass vials and ampoules.
• D. White (Translucent): Used for sharps, including needles, blades, scalpels, and other metal sharps in puncture-proof containers.

| BMW Color Code | Waste Category

| -------------- | --------------

| Yellow | Human anatomical waste, soiled waste, microbiological waste, expired medicines

| Red | Contaminated recyclable plastics (IV sets, tubing, catheters, urine bags, gloves, IV fluid bags)

| White (Translucent) | Sharps (needles, blades, scalpels)

| Blue | Glassware (vials, ampoules) and metallic implants
questions.learning: Red Understand the Biomedical Waste Management (BMWM) Rules, 2016 (amended) and identify the correct color-coded container for disposal of contaminated healthcare waste.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During your rural posting, you are asked to educate a small, uneducated village about the importance of routine antenatal care for pregnant mothers. You want to deliver some statistical data to emphasize its importance. Which of the following is the best way to do so?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pictogram

Pictogram is the best method of presenting data among people, who cannot understand orthodox charts.

In this method, small pictures or symbols are used to present the data. Fractions of the picture are used to represent numbers smaller than the value of a whole symbol. Basically, pictograms are a form of bar charts.

Other options

Option B- Line diagrams are mainly used to show the trend of events in a given period of time. For example trend of dengue cases in Asia during 2018-21.

Option C- Histogram is a pictorial diagram of a frequency distribution that consists of a series of blocks. The frequencies are given along the vertical axis and class intervals on the horizontal axis. The area of each block obtained is proportional to frequency.

Option D- Frequency polygon is the diagrammatical representation of frequency distribution obtained by joining the midpoints of the histogram blocks.

Pearl PF0302: Graphical Representation of Data

1. Histogram

* A histogram, by definition, is a graphical representation of frequency distribution that contains rectangles and shows the underlying frequency of a set of continuous, quantitative data.

* The X or horizontal axis is called the abscissa which usually has the group scores or class intervals of the variables/data and the Y or vertical axis is called the ordinate which usually shows the frequencies at which these variables appear.

* The following is a histogram of cholesterol levels from the Framingham Heart Study.

2. Bar Chart

* It is also called a bar graph.

* It is used mainly for nominal or ordinal scale data as they are not quantitative and usually qualitative.

* The difference between a bar graph and a histogram is that the rectangles are separated by spaces representing data that forms discrete categories instead of continuous groups.

* Bar graphs can be simple, multiple or component bar graphs.

3. Pie Charts

* Pie charts are also used for nominal or ordinal data.

* The categorical data are represented as segments of a circle.

4. Frequency polygons

* Frequency polygons are used for mainly ratio and interval scale data.

* In a frequency polygon, the mid-points of each class interval are joined together by straight lines.

5. Ogive

* A frequency polygon which is drawn to represent cumulative frequency distributions form a typical S-shaped curve which is called an ogive. It referred to as a cumulative frequency diagram.

6. Line chart

* It is also called a line diagram or line graph.

* Its best use is to show the trend of events or change over passage of time.
questions.learning: Pictogram Pictogram is the best method of presenting data among people, who cannot understand orthodox charts. In this method, small pictures or symbols are used to present the data.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text:
Which of the following are acid-fast staining organisms?

1. Nocardia
2. Mycobacterium leprae
3. Actinomyces
4. Cryptosporidium parvum
5. Isospora belli
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2, 4, 5

Nocardia, Mycobacterium leprae, Cryptosporidium parvum, and Cytoisospora belli (Options 1, 2, 4, and 5) are acid-fast staining organisms.

Acid-fast staining is based on the principle that tubercle bacilli resist decolorization with acids after staining with aniline dyes. Acid fastness is attributed to the variety of fatty acids, alcohols, and lipids in the tubercle bacilli. Acid-fast organisms usually contain mycolic acid, which is acid-fast in the free state.  The steps to carry out acid-fast staining as modified by Ziehl and Neelson are:

1. The slide is stained with carbolfuchsin along with the application of heat.
2. It is then decolorized with 20% sulphuric acid. Later methylene blue is used for counterstaining.
3. The acid-fast bacteria retain the fuchsin color, while other organisms take up the counterstain.

The genus Nocardia are aerobic organisms and weakly acid-fast positive rods. They stain with carbolfuchsin and retain it when 1-4% sulfuric acid is used.

Mycobacterium leprae, the causative agent of leprosy is a gram-positive bacillus. It is acid-fast when 5% sulphuric acid is used instead of 20%.

Cryptosporidium parvum, commonly causes diarrhea in immunocompromised individuals. The oocysts in the stool can be visualized by modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining. It appears as red acid-fast spheres. It can also be used for specimens such as sputum and bronchial wash.

Isospora belli is a coccidian parasite that can cause protracted diarrhea in immunocompromised patients. Modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining reveals pink-colored acid-fast oocyst in stool samples.

Actinomyces are gram-positive, anaerobic, and filamentous bacteria that are non-acid-fast in contrast to Nocardia.

questions.text: Which of the following anticoagulants requires coagulation profile monitoring?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lepirudin

Lepirudin (direct thrombin inhibitor) requires monitoring with aPTT.

Correct answer is B because lepirudin is a direct thrombin inhibitor with variable anticoagulant effect and requires monitoring using aPTT to maintain therapeutic range and avoid bleeding.

| Warfarin | Vitamin K antagonist | PT/INR

| Lepirudin | Direct thrombin inhibitor | aPTT

| Enoxaparin | Xa > Thrombin | SC | ❌

| Fondaparinux | Xa | SC | ❌

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Common site for congenital diaphragmatic hernia is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Posterolateral

Congenital diaphragmatic hernia most commonly occurs through the foramen of Bochdalek, a posterolateral defect of the diaphragm.

It results from failure of closure of the pleuroperitoneal membrane, leading to herniation of abdominal contents into the thoracic cavity.

Anterior defects (foramen of Morgagni) are less common and usually right-sided.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Which of the following may lead to a decrease in GFR?
options: Decrease in bowman capsule oncotic pressure
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Decrease in bowman capsule oncotic pressure

A decrease in bowman's capsule oncotic pressure would lead to a decrease in GFR.

Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is the volume of fluid filtered from the renal glomerular capillaries into the Bowman's capsule per unit time.

The GFR is determined by sum of the hydrostatic and colloid osmotic forces across the glomerular membrane, which gives the net filtration pressure. It is dependant on Glomerular Kf (glomerular ultrafiltration coefficient) also.

Mathematically, it can be expressed as follows:

GFR= Kf [PG + πB -PB- πG]

Forces favoring Filtration

• PG: Glomerular hydrostatic pressure
• πB: Bowman’s capsule oncotic pressure

Forces opposing Filtration

• PB: Bowman’s capsule hydrostatic pressure
• πG: Glomerular capillary oncotic pressure

Factors that can increase the GFR are as follows:

• Increase in glomerular capillary filtration coefficient Kf: This coefficient depends on the hydraulic conductivity and surface area of the glomerular capillaries.
• Decrease in Bowman's capsule hydrostatic pressure: Conditions with urinary tract obstruction can lead to an increase in this pressure and a fall in GFR.
• Decrease in glomerular colloid osmotic pressure: Accumulation of plasma proteins that are not filtered from the blood contributes to this pressure and an increase reduces the further filtration and GFR. It is directly proportional to the following factors:Arterial plasma colloid osmotic pressure
• Filtration fraction

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the most effective approach to managing mild nausea and vomiting in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: For the management of mild nausea and vomiting of pregnancy (morning sickness), lifestyle and dietary modifications are the recommended first-line treatments. This includes eating small, frequent meals throughout the day to avoid an empty stomach, which can trigger nausea. High-protein snacks and avoiding greasy or spicy foods are also beneficial. Increasing fluid intake (Option C) is important to prevent dehydration, but fluids should be taken between meals rather than with them to avoid over-distension of the stomach. Domperidone (Option B) and metoclopramide (Option D) are prokinetic medications that may be used in more persistent or severe cases (Hyperemesis Gravidarum), but they are not the "initial" approach for mild symptoms. Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) alone or in combination with doxylamine is the preferred first-line pharmacological agent if dietary changes are insufficient. Thus, simple behavioral and dietary adjustments remain the most effective starting point for mild symptoms
questions.learning: For the management of mild nausea and vomiting of pregnancy (morning sickness), lifestyle and dietary modifications are the recommended first-line treatments.
